units.title: User Rules
units.purpose: Define validation rules and domain constraints for User. Do NOT repeat data isolation (05), lifecycle states (02), or operation flows (03).
units.content: Users sign up for the application using an email address and password combination. Each user must provide a display name as part of their profile. The email address must be valid and unique across all users. Users can change their password at any time through their account settings. When a user chooses to delete their account, all their todos are permanently removed, including any items in the trash folder. This account deletion is irreversible and affects all data owned by that user. Login requires the same email and password credentials used during signup. Users cannot view or access another user's account or data under any circumstances.

sections.title: Email Signup Requirements
sections.content: Users sign up for the application using a valid email address and password combination. The email address must follow a standard email format with a local part, the @ symbol, and a domain name. Each email address can only be registered to one user account in the system. When a user attempts to register with an email that is already in use, the registration request is rejected. The system validates the email format during signup and displays an error if the format is incorrect. Users cannot reuse an email address that was previously deleted from the system.

sections.title: Password Creation Rules
sections.content: Users must create a password when signing up with their email address. The password is stored securely and cannot be viewed after creation. Users cannot use their display name or email address as their password. The password is required for login and cannot be empty. Users are prompted to confirm their password during signup to ensure accuracy.

sections.title: Display Name Configuration
sections.content: Each user must provide a display name as part of their profile during signup. The display name is shown to identify the user within the application. Users can edit their display name at any time through their profile settings. The display name cannot be empty and must contain at least one character. Users cannot set another user's display name as their own to avoid confusion.

sections.title: Password Change Capability
sections.content: Users can change their password at any time through their account settings. To change their password, users must enter their current password and a new password. The new password must differ from the current password. If the current password is incorrect, the password change request is rejected. After a successful password change, users must use the new password for all future logins.

sections.title: Account Deletion and Privacy
sections.content: Users can delete their account at any time through their account settings. When a user deletes their account, all their todos are permanently removed, including any items in the trash folder. This account deletion is irreversible and affects all data owned by that user. Users cannot view or access another user's account or data under any circumstances. Each user's todos are completely private and only accessible by the account owner. There is no way to view, access, or share another user's todos.

units.title: Todo Rules
units.purpose: Define validation rules and domain constraints for Todo. Do NOT repeat data isolation (05), lifecycle states (02), or operation flows (03).
units.content: Every todo must have a title, which is a required field when creating a new item. The description field is optional and can be left empty during creation. Users may optionally set a start date for each todo, but this is not required. Similarly, users may optionally set a due date for each todo without affecting creation. When a todo is first created, it is marked as incomplete by default. The system does not allow a todo to be created without a title. Todos belong exclusively to their owner and cannot be accessed by other users. Users can only view, edit, or delete their own todos, never those belonging to other users.

sections.title: Title Validation Requirements
sections.content: Every todo must have a title when created. The title field is required and cannot be left empty. If a user attempts to create a todo without providing a title, the request is rejected. The title can be updated later after creation, but the todo must always maintain a non-empty title value.

sections.title: Description Field Rules
sections.content: The description field is optional for todos. Users may leave the description empty when creating a todo. An empty description does not prevent todo creation. If a description is provided, it is stored with the todo for viewing. Users can update the description at any time or clear it by setting it to empty.

sections.title: Start Date Field Rules
sections.content: The start date field is optional for todos. Users may leave the start date empty when creating a todo. The system does not require a start date for todo creation. If a start date is set, it is displayed when viewing the todo. Users can update the start date after creation or clear it by setting it to empty. When sorting todos by start date, items without a start date appear at the end of the list.

sections.title: Due Date Field Rules
sections.content: The due date field is optional for todos. Users may leave the due date empty when creating a todo. The system does not require a due date for todo creation. If a due date is set, it is displayed when viewing the todo. Users can update the due date after creation or clear it by setting it to empty. When sorting todos by due date, items without a due date appear at the end of the list.

sections.title: Title and Due Date Relationship
sections.content: When both a start date and due date are provided for a todo, the due date must not be earlier than the start date. If a user sets a due date that precedes the start date, the request is rejected. This validation applies when creating a todo and when editing existing dates. Users must adjust the dates so the due date is on or after the start date before the change is accepted.

sections.title: Default Completion Status
sections.content: All newly created todos are marked as incomplete by default. There is no option to create a todo in a complete state. The incomplete status is the initial state for every todo regardless of other fields provided during creation. Users can change the completion status from incomplete to complete or vice versa after creation.

sections.title: Todo Ownership and Access Control
sections.content: Every todo belongs exclusively to the user who created it. Users can only view, edit, or delete their own todos. A user cannot access, modify, or delete another user's todos under any circumstances. The system enforces that todo operations are restricted to the owner only. If a non-owner attempts any operation on a todo, the request is rejected.

sections.title: Private Todo Access
sections.content: Each user's todos are completely private and invisible to other users. There is no mechanism to share todos between users or make todos public. Users cannot view, access, or browse another user's todos through any interface. The privacy boundary is absolute: each user sees only their own data.

sections.title: Owner-Only Modification
sections.content: Only the owner of a todo can modify its content. No other user can change a todo's title, description, dates, or completion status. Edit operations are validated against ownership, and non-owner edits are rejected. The system tracks edit history but only allows the owner to make changes.

sections.title: Creation Date Tracking
sections.content: Every todo has a creation date that is automatically recorded when the todo is created. This date represents when the todo first entered the system. The creation date cannot be modified after creation. It is displayed when viewing todos in the list view and when viewing individual todo details. The creation date is used for sorting options that order by creation date.

sections.title: Todo Status Toggle Rules
sections.content: Users can toggle a todo's completion status between complete and incomplete. This is a simple state change with no additional conditions. A complete todo can be marked incomplete, and an incomplete todo can be marked complete. The toggle operation requires no additional approval or validation beyond ownership.

sections.title: Todo Deletion Validation
sections.content: Users can only delete todos they own. Deleted todos are soft-deleted and moved to trash rather than permanently removed. The todo no longer appears in the normal todo list after deletion. Only the owner can delete their own todos. Attempts to delete another user's todo are rejected.

sections.title: Trash Operation Rules
sections.content: Users can view their deleted todos in the trash. Users can restore a deleted todo from trash, returning it to the normal todo list. Users can also permanently delete a todo from trash, which removes it and its edit history. Only the owner can perform trash operations on their own deleted todos.

units.title: EditHistoryEntry Rules
units.purpose: Define validation rules and domain constraints for EditHistoryEntry. Do NOT repeat data isolation (05), lifecycle states (02), or operation flows (03).
units.content: Every time a user modifies a todo, the system creates an edit history entry to record the change. Each history entry captures the timestamp when the edit was made. The history tracks what fields were changed, including title, description, start date, and due date. Only changed fields are recorded in each history entry; unchanged fields are not duplicated. The full edit history for a todo can be viewed by the todo owner. History entries are sorted with the most recent edits appearing first, followed by older changes in reverse chronological order. When a todo is permanently deleted from the trash, its entire edit history is also deleted. This deletion of history is permanent and cannot be recovered.

sections.title: Edit History Tracking
sections.content:
Every time a user modifies a todo, the system creates an edit history entry to record the change. This applies to any modification of the todo's title, description, start date, or due date.

Each edit history entry captures the exact moment when the edit was made. The timestamp records when the user's edit request was completed by the system.

Only fields that were actually changed are recorded in each history entry. If only the title was modified, only the title change is documented. The description, start date, and due date are not included in that entry if they remained unchanged. This prevents unnecessary duplication of unchanged values.

A history entry is created for every successful edit operation. The system tracks each modification as a separate entry in the todo's edit history. Users can view the complete edit history of any of their todos to see all past changes.

sections.title: Timestamp Recording
sections.content:
Each edit history entry includes a timestamp that records when the edit occurred. The timestamp captures the date and time when the user's edit request was processed by the system.

The timestamp is recorded automatically when the edit is completed. Users do not manually set the timestamp; it is generated by the system at the time of modification.

All timestamps are recorded in a consistent format that allows chronological ordering. This enables accurate sorting and retrieval of history entries based on their edit time.

sections.title: Field Change Documentation
sections.content:
When a todo's title is modified, the new title value is recorded in the edit history entry. The entry documents what the title was changed to, not the previous value.

When a todo's description is modified, the new description value is recorded in the edit history entry. The entry documents what the description was changed to. If the description was previously empty and is now populated, or vice versa, this change is captured.

When a todo's start date is modified, the new start date value is recorded in the edit history entry. The entry documents the date it was changed to. If the start date was previously unset and is now set, or vice versa, this change is captured.

When a todo's due date is modified, the new due date value is recorded in the edit history entry. The entry documents the date it was changed to. If the due date was previously unset and is now set, or vice versa, this change is captured.

Each field that is changed generates a record of what that field was changed to. The history tracks all modifications to all fields across all edits.

sections.title: Complete Edit History View
sections.content:
Users can view the full edit history of any todo that they own. The edit history displays all history entries that have been created for that todo.

The owner of a todo has visibility into all edit history entries for that todo. No other user can view another user's edit history, as todos and their associated history are private to their owner.

The edit history view shows each history entry with its timestamp and the fields that were changed. It provides a complete record of all modifications made to the todo since its creation.

sections.title: Recent to Oldest Sorting
sections.content:
History entries are sorted with the most recent edits appearing first. The entry created most recently is displayed at the top of the list.

Following the most recent entry, older edits appear in descending chronological order. The oldest entry appears at the bottom of the list.

This sorting ensures that users can immediately see the latest changes to a todo without needing to navigate to find them.

sections.title: Permanent History Deletion
sections.content:
When a todo is permanently deleted from the trash, its entire edit history is also deleted. All history entries associated with that todo are removed from the system.

This deletion of the edit history is permanent and cannot be recovered. Once a todo and its edit history are permanently deleted, there is no way to retrieve the deleted history entries.

The permanent deletion of a todo includes the deletion of all its edit history entries. Users should be aware that permanent deletion from the trash removes both the todo and all associated edit history.

units.title: List Browsing Expectations
units.purpose: Define business expectations for how users find, filter, and browse lists.
units.content: Define business expectations for how users find, filter, and browse lists.

sections.title: Filtering by Completion Status
sections.content:
Users can filter their todo list by completion status.
The available filter options are:
- All todos: Displays todos regardless of their completion status
- Complete todos: Displays only todos marked as complete
- Incomplete todos: Displays only todos marked as incomplete

When a filter is applied, the filtered results replace the unfiltered view.
Only the owner of a todo can view and filter their own todos.
There is no way to view or filter another user's todos.
If no filter is explicitly selected, the system displays all todos by default.

sections.title: Sorting by Date Fields
sections.content:
Users can sort their todo list by date fields.
The available sort options are:
- Creation date: Sort by when the todo was created (newest first or oldest first)
- Start date: Sort by the start date (earliest first or latest first)
- Due date: Sort by the due date (earliest first or latest first)

When sorting by start date or due date, todos without these dates are placed at the end of the list.
When sorting by creation date, todos without a creation date (edge case) are placed at the end of the list.
Users can toggle between ascending and descending order for each sort option.
Only one sort option can be active at a time.
If the user changes the sort option or direction, the list refreshes with the new ordering.

sections.title: Pagination Rules
sections.content:
Both the main todo list and the trash list are paginated.
Each page displays a fixed number of todos.
When viewing a paginated list, navigation controls allow users to move between pages.
Users can return to the first page or jump to the last page.
Pagination preserves any active filters and sort options across page changes.
When a todo is deleted or restored, the pagination may shift to maintain the list integrity.
If a filtered or sorted view returns zero results, an appropriate message is displayed.
The pagination does not affect the total count of todos available across all pages.

files.summary: Data ownership, privacy, retention, and recovery policies
files.content:
**multiUserTodoApp — Data ownership, privacy, retention, and recovery policies**

Data ownership, privacy, retention, and recovery policies

# Data Policies

Data ownership, privacy, retention, and recovery policies from a business perspective.

## Data Ownership and Privacy

Define who owns what data, who can access it, and privacy boundaries between users.

### Data Ownership

Each user owns all data created through their account, including todos and edit history.
Users have exclusive rights to their own todos and can manage them according to their preferences.
No other user or guest can claim ownership of another user's data.
Ownership is established upon account creation and persists until account deletion.

### Data Isolation

All user data is completely isolated between different users.
A user can only view, access, and modify their own todos and edit history.
There is no mechanism for viewing another user's data, regardless of invitation or sharing.
Guest users have no access to any user's private todos.

### Access Control

Users can only access their own todos and profile information.
Authentication is required to access any user data.
Once logged in, users can perform operations only on their own todos.
The system enforces strict boundaries between user data at all times.

### Profile Privacy

User profiles are private and belong exclusively to their owners.
Users can view and edit only their own profile information.
Users cannot view other users' profiles or profile information.
Display names are not visible to other users.

### Account Deletion

When a user deletes their account, all their data is permanently removed.
This includes all todos in the normal list, todos in trash, and all edit history entries.
Once deleted, the user's data cannot be recovered or restored.
Account deletion is a permanent action with immediate effect.

### No Data Sharing

The system does not support sharing todos between users.
There is no functionality to export, import, or transfer todos to other accounts.
Each user's data remains private and contained within their own account boundaries.

## Data Retention and Recovery

Define what happens to deleted data, how long it is retained, and how users can recover it.

### ### Soft Deletion Process

When a user deletes a todo, it is soft deleted and moved to the trash. The todo remains in the system but no longer appears in the normal todo list. The user can still view the deleted todo by accessing the trash view. Soft deleted todos retain all their original data including title, description, dates, and edit history.

### ### Trash Retention

Deleted todos remain in the trash indefinitely until the user chooses to restore or permanently delete them. There is no automatic expiration or retention period for items in the trash. Users retain full access to their soft deleted todos at any time.

### ### Recovery from Trash

Users can restore a deleted todo from the trash, which moves it back to the normal todo list. The restored todo retains all its original data including title, description, dates, completion status, and complete edit history. The restoration action is immediate and reversible.

### ### Permanent Deletion

Users can permanently delete a todo from the trash, which removes it from the system entirely. Permanent deletion is irreversible and cannot be undone. When a todo is permanently deleted, all associated edit history entries are also permanently deleted. The todo and its history are completely removed and cannot be recovered.

text:
I'll now design the database schema for your multi-user Todo application. Based on the requirements I analyzed, I need to create tables for:

1. **Users** - for authentication and account management
2. **UserProfiles** - for display names
3. **Todos** - for todo items with soft delete support
4. **TodoEditHistories** - to track every change to todos

Let me generate the complete database schema with Prisma ORM.

instruction:
Users table: id (UUID, primary key, auto-generated), email (unique, string, required), password (string, required, hashed), created_at (DateTime, required), updated_at (DateTime, required). Users can sign up, log in, change password, and delete account (including all todos).

UserProfiles table: id (UUID, primary key, auto-generated), user_id (UUID, foreign key to Users, required, unique), display_name (string, required), created_at (DateTime, required), updated_at (DateTime, required). Users have one profile with display name they can edit. Users cannot view other users' profiles.

Todos table: id (UUID, primary key, auto-generated), user_id (UUID, foreign key to Users, required, indexes for filtering), title (string, required), description (string, optional, default empty string), start_date (DateTime, optional), due_date (DateTime, optional), is_completed (Boolean, required, default false), created_at (DateTime, required, indexes for sorting), updated_at (DateTime, required), deleted_at (DateTime, optional, for soft delete). Newly created todos are incomplete. Deleted todos don't appear in normal list.

TodoEditHistories table: id (UUID, primary key, auto-generated), todo_id (UUID, foreign key to Todos, required, indexes), user_id (UUID, foreign key to Users, required), edited_at (DateTime, required), old_title (string, optional), new_title (string, optional), old_description (string, optional), new_description (string, optional), old_start_date (DateTime, optional), new_start_date (DateTime, optional), old_due_date (DateTime, optional), new_due_date (DateTime, optional). Every edit creates a history entry. Entries sorted by edited_at descending (most recent first).

Relationships:
- Users 1:1 UserProfiles
- Users 1:n Todos
- Users 1:n TodoEditHistories
- Todos 1:n TodoEditHistories

Business Rules:
- Users can only see their own todos (user_id foreign key ensures this)
- Soft delete: deleted_at is null for active todos, non-null for trash
- When permanently deleting a todo from trash, also delete its history entries
- Filter todos by completion status (is_completed: true/false/null for all)
- Sort by created_at, start_date, or due_date (null values appear last)

models.name: multi_user_todo_app_guests
models.description:
Guest user accounts for unauthenticated visitors to the multi-user todo application.

This table stores temporary guest identities identified by email and password, allowing unauthenticated users to access the system before completing registration. Each guest account is associated with a specific device through session tracking in the multi_user_todo_app_guest_sessions table.

Key relationships:
- One-to-many with multi_user_todo_app_guest_sessions for session tracking
- Guests can upgrade to member accounts via email/password registration

Business context:
- Guest accounts serve as entry point for unauthenticated users
- Guest data is isolated from member data
- Guest accounts are created during initial app access
- Passwords are hashed for security before storage
- Soft delete capability for account lifecycle management

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Guest email address used for identification and authentication.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for guest account authentication.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last guest account update.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of soft deletion, null when active.

models.name: multi_user_todo_app_guest_sessions
models.description:
Temporary session tokens for guest access using device_id and fingerprint.

This table tracks unauthenticated visitor sessions to maintain state across requests before guest registration. Each session is linked to a guest account via device fingerprint for session continuity and security.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to {@link multi_user_todo_app_guests} - one guest can have multiple active sessions
- Sessions expire based on expired_at timestamp for security
- Managed through authentication middleware, not direct user CRUD

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_app_guest_id
foreignFields.description: Guest account this session belongs to. {@link multi_user_todo_app_guests.id}

plainFields.name: device_id
plainFields.description: Device identifier for guest session continuity across requests.

plainFields.name: fingerprint
plainFields.description: Device fingerprint hash for session security and fraud detection.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Client IP address for session tracking and security auditing.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Last known page URL for session context.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL from the request for session source tracking.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session expiration timestamp for security cleanup.

models.name: multi_user_todo_app_members
models.description:
Registered member user accounts with email/password authentication credentials.

This table serves as the primary identity record for authenticated members in the system. Each member account stores the email address and hashed password required for authentication, along with temporal tracking fields for audit and soft delete capabilities.

Members are distinct from guests in that they have persistent accounts that can be authenticated and can access their private todo list, edit history, and trash functionality. JWT session tokens for member authentication with access and refresh token support.

This table tracks all active member login sessions, storing authentication tokens and connection metadata for security auditing. Each session represents a single authenticated device/browser combination with a unique JWT access token and refresh token pair.

- Multiple sessions per member allowed (mobile, web, tablet)

- Tokens stored for refresh and re-authentication
- Expired sessions are identified by expired_at timestamp
- Member logout or password changes may invalidate sessions

**Security Considerations:**
- Access tokens used for API authentication
- Refresh tokens used to obtain new access tokens
- Connection metadata (IP, referrer) stored for fraud detection
- Multiple concurrent sessions supported per member

- Sessions are managed through authentication flows, not direct CRUD
- Expired_at field enables automatic cleanup of stale sessions

Stores temporary cryptographic tokens that members receive when requesting password reset via email. Each token is tied to a specific member account and expires after a configured time window (typically 1-24 hours). models.name: multi_user_todo_app_todo_edit_histories

plainFields.name: new_description
plainFields.description: Description value after the edit. Null if description was removed in this edit.

plainFields.name: new_start_date

plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp. Used for auditing and chronological ordering.

plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp. Maintained for consistency with other tables.

### `multi_user_todo_app_guests`

Guest user accounts for unauthenticated visitors to the multi-user todo
application.

This table stores temporary guest identities identified by email and
password, allowing unauthenticated users to access the system before
completing registration. Each guest account is associated with a specific
device through session tracking in the multi_user_todo_app_guest_sessions
table.

Key relationships:
- One-to-many with multi_user_todo_app_guest_sessions for session tracking
- Guests can upgrade to member accounts via email/password registration

Business context:
- Guest accounts serve as entry point for unauthenticated users
- Guest data is isolated from member data
- Guest accounts are created during initial app access
- Passwords are hashed for security before storage
- Soft delete capability for account lifecycle management

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`: Guest email address used for identification and authentication.
- `password_hash`: Hashed password for guest account authentication.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the guest account was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of the last guest account update.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp of soft deletion, null when active.

### `multi_user_todo_app_guest_sessions`

Temporary session tokens for guest access using device_id and fingerprint.

This table tracks unauthenticated visitor sessions to maintain state
across requests before guest registration. Each session is linked to a
guest account via device fingerprint for session continuity and security.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to [multi_user_todo_app_guests](#multi_user_todo_app_guests) - one guest can have
multiple active sessions
- Sessions expire based on expired_at timestamp for security
- Managed through authentication middleware, not direct user CRUD

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `multi_user_todo_app_guest_id`
  > Guest account this session belongs to. {@link
  > multi_user_todo_app_guests.id}
- `device_id`: Device identifier for guest session continuity across requests.
- `fingerprint`: Device fingerprint hash for session security and fraud detection.
- `ip`: Client IP address for session tracking and security auditing.
- `href`: Last known page URL for session context.
- `referrer`: Referrer URL from the request for session source tracking.
- `created_at`: Session creation timestamp.
- `expired_at`: Session expiration timestamp for security cleanup.

### `multi_user_todo_app_members`

Registered member user accounts with email/password authentication
credentials.

This table serves as the primary identity record for authenticated
members in the system. Each member account stores the email address and
hashed password required for authentication, along with temporal tracking
fields for audit and soft delete capabilities.

Members are distinct from guests in that they have persistent accounts
that can be authenticated and can access their private todo list, edit
history, and trash functionality. This table is referenced by the
multi_user_todo_app_member_sessions table for session management and
multi_user_todo_app_member_password_resets for password reset flows.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`: Unique email address used for member login and account identification.
- `password_hash`
  > Bcrypt-hashed password string for member authentication. Never stored in
  > plaintext.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the member account was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the member account was last updated.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete timestamp. NULL indicates active account, non-NULL indicates
  > deleted account awaiting permanent removal.

### `multi_user_todo_app_member_sessions`

JWT session tokens for member authentication with access and refresh
token support.

This table tracks all active member login sessions, storing
authentication tokens and connection metadata for security auditing. Each
session represents a single authenticated device/browser combination with
a unique JWT access token and refresh token pair.

**Key Relationships:**
- Belongs to one member: [multi_user_todo_app_members](#multi_user_todo_app_members) (via
multi_user_todo_app_member_id)
- Multiple sessions per member allowed (mobile, web, tablet)
- Sessions are append-only audit records - never modified after creation

**Session Lifecycle:**
- Created on successful member login
- Tokens stored for refresh and re-authentication
- Expired sessions are identified by expired_at timestamp
- Member logout or password changes may invalidate sessions

**Security Considerations:**
- Access tokens used for API authentication
- Refresh tokens used to obtain new access tokens
- Connection metadata (IP, referrer) stored for fraud detection
- Multiple concurrent sessions supported per member

**Usage Pattern:**
- Members can maintain multiple active sessions simultaneously
- Sessions are managed through authentication flows, not direct CRUD
- Expired_at field enables automatic cleanup of stale sessions

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `multi_user_todo_app_member_id`
  > Belonged member's [multi_user_todo_app_members.id](#multi_user_todo_app_members). Required for
  > session ownership and token validation.
- `access_token`
  > JWT access token for API authentication. Used to authorize member
  > requests. Stored as hash for security.
- `refresh_token`
  > JWT refresh token for obtaining new access tokens. Valid until expired_at
  > timestamp.
- `ip`
  > Client IP address from request headers. Used for connection metadata and
  > security auditing.
- `href`
  > Request URL path from browser. Captures which page/route triggered the
  > login.
- `referrer`
  > HTTP referrer header value. Used to track login source and detect
  > suspicious redirects.
- `created_at`
  > Session creation timestamp. When the member successfully authenticated
  > and this session was created.
- `expired_at`
  > Session expiration timestamp. After this time, tokens are invalid.
  > Security: NOT NULL by default.

### `multi_user_todo_app_member_password_resets`

Password reset tokens for member account recovery flow.

Stores temporary cryptographic tokens that members receive when
requesting password reset via email. Each token is tied to a specific
member account and expires after a configured time window (typically 1-24
hours). This table enables secure password recovery without exposing the
member's actual password.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to exactly one [multi_user_todo_app_members](#multi_user_todo_app_members) account via
member_id
- Tokens are single-use: when a reset is completed, the token is marked
as deleted
- Expired tokens remain in the table until garbage collection (soft
delete pattern)

Behavioral notes:
- Only one active reset token per member at a time (enforced by unique
member_id constraint)
- Requesting a new reset automatically invalidates previous tokens
- Tokens are never stored in plain text; only hashed values are used for
comparison
- The table maintains audit trail of all reset attempts including
successful, expired, and unused tokens

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `member_id`
  > Member account's [multi_user_todo_app_members.id](#multi_user_todo_app_members) that requested
  > the password reset.
- `token`
  > Cryptographic reset token value. This is a hashed representation of the
  > actual token sent to the member's email. The plain token is generated
  > during reset request and compared against this hashed value during
  > validation.
- `expired_at`
  > Timestamp when this reset token expires and becomes invalid. Tokens
  > typically expire after 1-24 hours depending on security configuration.
  > Must not be null to enforce token lifecycle.
- `created_at`
  > Creation timestamp when this reset token was generated and sent to the
  > member.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for this reset token record.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete timestamp. When null, token is active. When set, token has
  > been consumed (password reset completed), expired, or manually
  > invalidated.

### `multi_user_todo_app_todos`

Main todo entity for authenticated member accounts.

Represents individual todo items that members create and manage in their
private todo list. Each todo has a title, optional description, optional
start date, optional due date, and completion status. Supports soft
delete for trash functionality where deleted todos are hidden from normal
list but can be restored or permanently removed.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to one member via user_id [multi_user_todo_app_members.id](#multi_user_todo_app_members)
- Has many edit history entries {@link
multi_user_todo_app_todo_edit_histories.id}

Behavioral notes:
- Soft delete: deleted_at is null for active todos, non-null for trash items
- New todos are created with is_completed = false by default
- Members can only see and manage their own todos (enforced by user_id
foreign key)

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `user_id`: Owner member's [multi_user_todo_app_members.id](#multi_user_todo_app_members).
- `title`: Todo title. Required field.
- `description`: Optional todo description. Defaults to empty string.
- `start_date`: Optional start date for the todo.
- `due_date`: Optional due date for the todo.
- `is_completed`: Whether the todo is completed. Defaults to false.
- `created_at`: Todo creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last todo update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp. Null for active todos, non-null for trash items.

### `multi_user_todo_app_todo_edit_histories`

Audit trail table that captures every edit made to todos, storing before
and after values for all editable fields.

This snapshot table serves as a complete history log for todo
modifications, enabling users to review changes over time. Each edit
creates a new history entry with old and new values for title,
description, start_date, and due_date fields.

The table maintains referential integrity through foreign keys to the
owning todo and the user who performed the edit. Entries are typically
queried in descending order by edited_at to show the most recent changes
first.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_id`: The todo that was edited. [multi_user_todo_app_todos.id](#multi_user_todo_app_todos)
- `user_id`: The user who performed the edit. [multi_user_todo_app_members.id](#multi_user_todo_app_members)
- `edited_at`
  > Timestamp when the edit occurred. Used for sorting history entries by
  > recency.
- `old_title`: Title value before the edit. Null if title was added in this edit.
- `new_title`: Title value after the edit. Null if title was removed in this edit.
- `old_description`
  > Description value before the edit. Null if description was added in this
  > edit.
- `new_description`
  > Description value after the edit. Null if description was removed in this
  > edit.
- `old_start_date`
  > Start date value before the edit. Null if start_date was added or was
  > null before this edit.
- `new_start_date`
  > Start date value after the edit. Null if start_date was removed or set to
  > null in this edit.
- `old_due_date`
  > Due date value before the edit. Null if due_date was added or was null
  > before this edit.
- `new_due_date`
  > Due date value after the edit. Null if due_date was removed or set to
  > null in this edit.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp. Used for auditing and chronological ordering.
- `updated_at`
  > Record last update timestamp. Maintained for consistency with other
  > tables.

text: I'll now design the API interface specification for your multi-user Todo application. Based on the database schema, I'll create comprehensive API endpoints with OpenAPI schemas and TypeScript interfaces.

instruction:
Authentication & Account Endpoints:

POST /api/auth/signup
- Body: { email: string, password: string, displayName: string }
- Returns: { user: { id: string, email: string, createdAt: string }, profile: { id: string, displayName: string }, token: string }
- Validations: email format, password minimum 6 characters, display name required
- Description: Create a new user account

POST /api/auth/login
- Body: { email: string, password: string }
- Returns: { user: { id: string, email: string, createdAt: string }, profile: { id: string, displayName: string }, token: string }
- Description: Login with email and password, returns JWT token

PUT /api/auth/password
- Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
- Body: { currentPassword: string, newPassword: string }
- Returns: { success: boolean }
- Description: Change user password

DELETE /api/auth/account
- Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
- Returns: { success: boolean }
- Description: Delete user account and all their todos (including trash), permanently

User Profile Endpoints:

GET /api/profile
- Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
- Returns: { id: string, displayName: string, createdAt: string, updatedAt: string }
- Description: Get current user's profile (users cannot view other users' profiles)

PUT /api/profile
- Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
- Body: { displayName: string }
- Returns: { id: string, displayName: string, updatedAt: string }
- Description: Update current user's display name

Todo CRUD Endpoints:

POST /api/todos
- Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
- Body: { title: string, description?: string, startDate?: string, dueDate?: string }
- Returns: { id: string, title: string, description: string, startDate: string | null, dueDate: string | null, isCompleted: boolean, createdAt: string }
- Validations: title required, description can be empty string
- Description: Create a new todo (incomplete by default)

GET /api/todos
- Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
- Query params: 
  - page: number (default 1, min 1)
  - limit: number (default 10, min 1, max 100)
  - status: 'all' | 'completed' | 'incomplete' (default 'all')
  - sortBy: 'createdAt' | 'startDate' | 'dueDate' (default 'createdAt')
  - sortOrder: 'asc' | 'desc' (default 'desc')
- Returns: { items: Todo[], totalCount: number, page: number, limit: number }
- Description: List todos with pagination, filtering by completion status, and sorting
- Sorting rules: null dates appear last when sorting by startDate or dueDate

GET /api/todos/:id
- Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
- Returns: { id: string, title: string, description: string, startDate: string | null, dueDate: string | null, isCompleted: boolean, createdAt: string, updatedAt: string }
- Description: Get a single todo by ID (only user's own todos)

PUT /api/todos/:id
- Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
- Body: { title?: string, description?: string, startDate?: string, dueDate?: string }
- Returns: { id: string, title: string, description: string, startDate: string | null, dueDate: string | null, isCompleted: boolean, createdAt: string, updatedAt: string }
- Validations: title cannot be empty if provided
- Description: Update a todo (creates edit history entry)
- Note: Every edit is recorded in history

PATCH /api/todos/:id/complete
- Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
- Returns: { id: string, isCompleted: boolean, updatedAt: string }
- Description: Toggle todo completion status (incomplete → complete, complete → incomplete)

DELETE /api/todos/:id (soft delete)
- Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
- Returns: { id: string, deletedAt: string }
- Description: Soft delete a todo (moves to trash, doesn't appear in normal list)

Trash Endpoints:

GET /api/todos/trash
- Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
- Query params:
  - page: number (default 1, min 1)
  - limit: number (default 10, min 1, max 100)
- Returns: { items: { id: string, title: string, description: string, deletedAt: string }[], totalCount: number, page: number, limit: number }
- Description: List deleted todos (trash)

PUT /api/todos/:id/restore
- Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
- Returns: { id: string, title: string, description: string, startDate: string | null, dueDate: string | null, isCompleted: boolean, createdAt: string, updatedAt: string }
- Description: Restore a todo from trash (returns to normal list, deleted_at is cleared)

DELETE /api/todos/:id (permanent delete from trash)
- Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
- Returns: { success: boolean }
- Description: Permanently delete a todo from trash (also deletes its edit history)

Edit History Endpoints:

GET /api/todos/:id/history
- Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
- Returns: { items: { id: string, editedAt: string, oldTitle: string | null, newTitle: string | null, oldDescription: string | null, newDescription: string | null, oldStartDate: string | null, newStartDate: string | null, oldDueDate: string | null, newDueDate: string | null }[], totalCount: number }
- Description: Get edit history for a todo, sorted by editedAt descending (most recent first)
- Each history entry records what fields changed

operations.specification: Create a new guest account by validating email format, checking email uniqueness against the guests table, hashing the password using bcrypt, and creating a new guest record with the provided email, hashed password, and display_name. After successful account creation, generate a JWT session token by creating a record in the guest_sessions table with access_token and refresh_token derived from the guest_id and device fingerprint. operations.description:
User Registration - This endpoint allows unauthenticated visitors to create a new guest account in the multi-user todo application by providing their email address, password, and display name. The email address is validated for proper format using standard email validation patterns and must be unique across all guest accounts in the multi_user_todo_app_guests table. If the email format is invalid or the email is already registered, the request is rejected with an appropriate error.

The password is required and must be securely hashed using bcrypt before being stored in the password field of the guest record. Upon successful account creation, the system automatically generates a JWT session by creating an entry in the multi_user_todo_app_guest_sessions table with both access_token and refresh_token values derived from the guest_id and device fingerprint information. This session enables the newly registered guest to perform authenticated operations immediately after registration.

The display_name becomes the guest's visible identifier across the application and is stored in the display_name field. This endpoint returns the complete guest account information including the generated authentication token, allowing the client to immediately begin using the authenticated features of the application without a separate login step.

responseBody.description: Authenticated guest account with session token

operations.specification: Validate the provided refresh token by looking up the corresponding guest_sessions record in the database using the refresh_token field. If the token is valid and not expired, generate a new access_token by creating a new session record with a fresh access_token and refresh_token pair derived from the guest_id and device fingerprint. Invalidate the old refresh token to prevent replay attacks. Return the new access token to the client.
operations.description:
Token Refresh - This endpoint allows guests to renew their expired JWT session tokens without requiring re-authentication. Guests receive both access_token and refresh_token during registration via the join operation. The refresh_token is used to obtain new access tokens when the original access token expires.

The system validates the refresh token by querying the multi_user_todo_app_guest_sessions table for a matching refresh_token record. The token must be valid (not expired, not previously invalidated) and associated with an active guest account in the multi_user_todo_app_guests table. If the token is invalid, expired, or has been used, the refresh request is rejected.

Upon successful validation, the system generates a new access_token and refresh_token pair by creating a new guest_sessions record. The old refresh token is invalidated to prevent replay attacks. This ensures that each refresh token can only be used once, maintaining the security of the session. The client receives the new access token and should replace the old one for subsequent authenticated requests.

responseBody.description: New session token for the guest

Login endpoint for member account authentication using email and password credentials. This operation validates the member's credentials against the stored values in the multi_user_todo_app_members table and issues JWT session tokens for authenticated API access.

operations.description:
Token refresh endpoint for renewing expired JWT access tokens without re-authentication. This operation allows members to obtain new access tokens using a valid refresh token from the multi_user_todo_app_member_sessions table, eliminating the need to re-enter credentials.

The multi_user_todo_app_member_sessions table contains session records with access_token, refresh_token, member_id, device_fingerprint, created_at, and expires_at fields. The system validates that the provided refresh_token matches a stored session record, verifies the member_id and device_fingerprint match the original session, and checks that the token has not expired.

Upon successful validation, the system generates new JWT tokens (access_token with 1-hour expiration, refresh_token with 7-day expiration), stores them in the sessions table, and invalidates the old refresh token to prevent token reuse. This enables seamless authentication without requiring members to log in again.

operations.description:
Update the current authenticated user's display name in their profile.

This operation allows a member user to modify their display name, which is the name that identifies them within the multi-user todo application. The display name is shown throughout the system to identify the user and can be updated at any time through their profile settings.

The request must include a valid Bearer authentication token in the Authorization header. Only the profile owner can update their own display name; cross-user profile access is strictly prohibited for privacy reasons. Users cannot set their display name to an empty value or a value containing only whitespace.

Display name changes are immediately reflected in the user's profile and are permanent. The system validates that the new display name contains at least one character before persisting the update.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Authenticate the request using Bearer token from Authorization header.

Validate the token belongs to an active member session.

Extract the member_id from the authenticated session.

Parse the request body to extract the displayName field.

Validate displayName is not empty and not whitespace-only.

Validate displayName does not conflict with existing users.

Execute UPDATE query on multi_user_todo_app_members table:
  - Set displayName = new value
  - Set updatedAt = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
  - WHERE member_id = authenticated_member_id

Return the updated profile record with id, displayName, and updatedAt.

If authentication fails, return 401 Unauthorized.
If validation fails, return 400 Bad Request with specific error.
If update fails, return 500 Internal Server Error.

responseBody.description: The updated user profile containing the new display name

requestBody.description: Profile update request containing the new display name

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of the authenticated member's active sessions.

This operation allows users to view all their login sessions across devices, including session metadata such as device identifier, client IP address, referrer URL, and creation timestamps. Sessions are used for authentication tracking and security auditing.

Each session represents a single authenticated device or browser combination. The system supports multiple concurrent sessions per member, enabling users to log in from multiple devices simultaneously (e.g., mobile phone, desktop, tablet).

The operation supports filtering by session status (active/expired), date range for session creation, and device identifier patterns. Results are paginated to handle large session histories efficiently.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query multi_user_todo_app_member_sessions table for the authenticated member.

Filtering criteria:
- Filter by session status: active (expired_at >= current time) or expired
- Filter by creation date range: created_at between start and end
- Filter by device_id pattern match (partial matching)
- Filter by IP address pattern match

Pagination:
- Use cursor-based or offset-based pagination
- Default page size: 10, maximum: 100
- Sort by created_at descending (newest sessions first)

Join requirements:
- No joins required - all session data is in the member_sessions table
- Belongs to member table but member details not needed for this operation

Security:
- Filter by authenticated member's ID (multi_user_todo_app_member_id)
- Users can only view their own sessions
- Return summary information (hide sensitive token data)

Edge cases:
- Return empty array if no sessions exist
- Handle expired_at null or past timestamps correctly
- Validate pagination parameters (min 1, max 100)

responseBody.description: Paginated list of session summaries

requestBody.description: Session listing filter criteria and pagination parameters

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific authentication session for the authenticated member from the multi_user_todo_app_member_sessions table.

This operation returns metadata about a member's login session including the session creation timestamp, expiration timestamp, connection information (IP address, browser path, referrer source), and session status. The session data is used for security auditing, session management, and allowing members to monitor their active logins across different devices.

The session owner (the member who created this session) is the only authorized actor who can view this session's details. Attempting to access another member's session results in an authorization error. This enforces the privacy policy that authentication metadata is isolated to each user account. Each session is linked to a member through the multi_user_todo_app_member_id foreign key.

The response includes the session's unique identifier, the member's ID, the IP address from the original request, the URL path (href) that was accessed during login, the referrer header value, creation timestamp, and expiration timestamp. Note that sensitive token values (access_token, refresh_token) are stored as hashes and are not returned in the API response for security reasons.

Sessions are managed automatically through the authentication system. This endpoint provides read-only access to session metadata for purposes such as displaying active sessions in the user interface, identifying suspicious login activity, or preparing for session termination via the logout operation. Sessions are append-only audit records that are never modified after creation.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
1. Validate that the requesting user is authenticated (has valid session token).
2. Extract sessionId from path parameter and validate it is a valid UUID format.
3. Query multi_user_todo_app_member_sessions table for record with matching id.
4. Verify that the retrieved session belongs to the authenticated member (multi_user_todo_app_member_id == authenticated_user_id).
5. If session not found, return 404 Not Found error.
6. If session does not belong to authenticated user, return 403 Forbidden error.
7. Return session metadata (id, memberId, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at) without token values.
8. Session status (active/expired) is determined by comparing expired_at to current server time.

Database Query:
SELECT id, multi_user_todo_app_member_id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at
FROM multi_user_todo_app_member_sessions
WHERE id = :sessionId AND multi_user_todo_app_member_id = :userId

responseBody.description: Detailed session information including connection metadata and timestamps

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the session to retrieve
parameters.name: sessionId

operations.description:
Create a new todo item in the authenticated user's todo list.

This operation allows members to create new todo items with a title and optional fields including description, start date, and due date. Todos are created in incomplete state by default and appear in the user's active todo list immediately upon creation.

The title field is required and must not be empty. The description, start date, and due date fields are optional. If not provided, description defaults to an empty string and dates are set to null.

Every edit made to a todo (including this initial creation) is automatically recorded in the edit history table. Each edit history entry captures the before and after values of all modified fields, providing a complete audit trail of changes.

Authentication is required via Bearer token. Only authenticated members can create todos; guests cannot access this endpoint.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Insert a new record into multi_user_todo_app_todos table.

1. Validate authentication: Verify Bearer token in Authorization header belongs to a member (not guest)
2. Validate request body:
   - title: required, non-empty string
   - description: optional, can be empty string or omitted (default to empty string)
   - startDate: optional ISO date string or omitted
   - dueDate: optional ISO date string or omitted
3. Set isCompleted to false (default incomplete state)
4. Generate unique UUID for id field
5. Set createdAt and updatedAt to current timestamp (UTC)
6. Insert record into multi_user_todo_app_todos table
7. Create initial EditHistoryEntry record in multi_user_todo_app_todo_edit_histories table:
   - Reference the newly created todo by id
   - Store oldTitle as null, newTitle as provided title
   - Store oldDescription as null, newDescription as provided description
   - Store oldStartDate as null, newStartDate as provided startDate
   - Store oldDueDate as null, newDueDate as provided dueDate
   - Set editedAt to current timestamp
8. Return the full created todo object with all fields including id, createdAt, updatedAt

Error handling:
- Return 401 if authentication token is invalid or expired
- Return 403 if user is a guest (not authenticated member)
- Return 400 if title is missing or empty
- Return 400 if required validation fails

responseBody.description: The newly created todo with all fields

requestBody.description: Creation data for the new todo item

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of todo items belonging to the authenticated user.

This operation provides advanced list browsing capabilities for the user's private todo list. It supports filtering by completion status (active, completed, or all todos) and flexible sorting options based on creation date, start date, or due date. The response includes paginated results with metadata for navigating large result sets.

Each todo in the response contains essential information including title, description, date fields, and completion status. Users can only view their own todos—privacy and ownership boundaries are strictly enforced through user_id matching.

The endpoint handles null values in optional date fields (start_date and due_date) with special sorting behavior: when sorting by these fields, todos with missing dates appear last in the result set regardless of sort order.

Successful completion of a todo operation requires prior authentication. The user must provide a valid JWT token in the Authorization header. Unauthorized requests are rejected with appropriate error responses.

For detailed information about a single todo, use GET /todos/{id}. For creating new todos, use POST /todos. For editing existing todos, use PUT /todos/{id}. For viewing edit history, use GET /todos/{id}/history.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query multi_user_todo_app_todos table filtered by user_id (current authenticated user) and deleted_at IS NULL (excluding trash items).

Apply filters:
- status filter: 'all' returns todos where deleted_at IS NULL, 'completed' filters where is_completed = true, 'incomplete' filters where is_completed = false

Apply pagination:
- Extract page and limit from requestBody
- Calculate offset as (page - 1) * limit
- Use LIMIT limit and OFFSET offset for database query

Apply sorting:
- sortBy parameter determines ORDER BY clause: 'createdAt' uses created_at, 'startDate' uses start_date, 'dueDate' uses due_date
- sortOrder determines direction: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending
- For start_date and due_date sorting, use COALESCE to handle NULL values: ORDER BY CASE WHEN start_date IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, start_date DESC
- Default sorting is by created_at descending

Return paginated response with:
- items array containing Todo.ISummary objects
- totalCount: count of matching records (for pagination metadata)
- page, limit: pagination parameters from request

Error handling:
- Throw NotFound if user_id does not match current user
- Throw ValidationError for invalid page (min 1), limit (1-100), status values, sortBy values, or sortOrder values

responseBody.description: Paginated list of todo items with metadata

operations.description:
Retrieve a single todo by its unique identifier from the authenticated member's todo list.

This operation returns complete todo information including the todo's title, description, start date, due date, completion status, and timestamps. The todo must exist in the user's account and belong to the authenticated member for the request to succeed.

The system enforces strict privacy and ownership boundaries - users can only view their own todos. Any attempt to access another user's todo by ID will be rejected. The todo must exist in the database and be associated with the current user's account.

This operation is typically used when a user clicks on a specific todo from their todo list to view or edit its details. It requires the authenticated member to provide a valid JWT token in the Authorization header.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query multi_user_todo_app_todos table for a todo with the specified ID.

1. Extract JWT token from Authorization header and validate authentication
2. Resolve the member_id from the authenticated token
3. Query multi_user_todo_app_todos WHERE id = {todoId} AND member_id = {authenticated_member_id}
4. If no todo found, return 404 Not Found error
5. Return todo data with all fields: id, title, description, startDate, dueDate, isCompleted, createdAt, updatedAt
6. Do not return any todos that don't belong to the authenticated member

Error handling:
- 404 if todo doesn't exist or doesn't belong to user
- 401 if no valid authentication token provided

Data transformation:
- Convert database record to Todo response object
- Ensure null dates are represented as null (not empty strings)
- Maintain ISO 8601 datetime format for dates

responseBody.description: Complete todo information with all fields

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the todo to retrieve
parameters.name: todoId

operations.description:
Update an existing todo in the authenticated member's todo list.

This operation modifies one or more fields of a todo belonging to the current member. The todo must exist in the member's account and belong to the current authenticated user. The system validates ownership for every update operation by checking that the todo is associated with the member's account.

Every update automatically creates an EditHistoryEntry record that tracks which fields changed and their previous values. This audit trail is preserved even when the todo is moved to trash or deleted. The edit history provides a complete chronology of changes to the todo throughout its lifecycle.

The title field cannot be updated to an empty string if provided. Description, start date, and due date can be updated to any valid value including null. The isCompleted field cannot be modified through this operation; use the toggle completion endpoint instead.

Related operations include GET /todos/{todoId} to retrieve current todo information, PATCH /todos/{todoId}/complete to toggle completion status, and GET /todos/{todoId}/history to view the edit history for this todo.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Verify the current user is authenticated as a member (not guest)
2. Query multi_user_todo_app_todos table for record with id = todoId
3. Verify ownership: todo.user_id must match current member's id
4. Validate request body:
   - If title is provided, it must not be empty (non-zero length)
   - startDate and dueDate must be valid ISO 8601 date strings if provided
5. Build update set from provided fields (title, description, startDate, dueDate)
6. Perform UPDATE on multi_user_todo_app_todos table with new values
7. Update updatedAt timestamp to current time
8. Create EditHistoryEntry record in multi_user_todo_app_todo_edit_histories:
   - Store old values from before update
   - Store new values from update request
   - Set editedAt to current time
   - Only record fields that actually changed
9. Return the updated todo record with all fields including new updatedAt value

Edge cases:
- Todo not found: return 404 Not Found
- Todo belongs to different user: return 403 Forbidden
- Title is empty string: return 400 Bad Request

responseBody.description: The updated todo object with all current field values including the new updatedAt timestamp

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the todo to update
parameters.name: todoId

requestBody.description: Partial todo data containing any fields to update. All fields are optional, but at least one must be provided.

operations.description:
Toggles a todo's completion status between complete and incomplete.

This operation allows users to mark a todo as complete or mark a completed todo as incomplete. The toggle is a simple state change with no additional validation conditions beyond ownership verification.

When the completion status is toggled, the system automatically creates an EditHistoryEntry to record the change. This provides an audit trail of all status modifications per the edit history tracking requirements.

Only authenticated members can toggle the status of todos that belong to their account. The system validates that the todo exists in the user's account before performing the toggle operation.

The response includes the updated todo with the new isCompleted status and the updated timestamp.
operations.name: complete
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the request - verify member JWT token
2. Extract todoId from path parameter
3. Query multi_user_todo_app_todos for the todo record
4. Validate: todo exists AND todo.memberId equals the authenticated member's ID
5. If validation fails, return 404 Not Found or 403 Forbidden
6. Toggle isCompleted field: if true then false, if false then true
7. Update updatedAt timestamp to current UTC datetime
8. Insert new record into multi_user_todo_app_todo_edit_histories with:
   - todoId: the todo ID
   - editedAt: current UTC datetime
   - Track old vs new isCompleted values in appropriate fields
9. Return updated todo record with new isCompleted and updatedAt values

Edge cases:
- Todo does not exist: return 404
- Todo belongs to another member: return 403 Forbidden
- Concurrent updates: use database transaction or optimistic locking

operations.description:
Soft delete a todo by moving it to the trash.

This operation permanently removes a todo from the active todo list by setting the deleted_at timestamp to the current datetime. The todo remains in the system and can be viewed in the trash, restored, or permanently deleted.

The operation enforces strict ownership validation - users can only delete their own todos. Any attempt to delete another user's todo is rejected with an authorization error.

The todo's edit history entries remain intact during soft deletion. They are only permanently removed when the todo is permanently deleted from the trash using the trash deletion endpoint.

Related operations:
- GET /todos/{todoId}: View todo details before deletion
- GET /todos/trash: View deleted todos in trash
- PUT /todos/{todoId}/restore: Restore a deleted todo back to the active list
- DELETE /todos/{todoId} (permanent): Permanently delete from trash (also deletes edit history)
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Validate authentication - require valid member session token
2. Extract todoId from path parameter (UUID format)
3. Query multi_user_todo_app_todos for record matching todoId AND user_id = authenticated user's ID
4. If record not found, return 404 Not Found
5. Check if deleted_at is already non-null - if todo is already in trash, return 409 Conflict
6. Set deleted_at to current UTC timestamp
7. Update updated_at to current UTC timestamp
8. Commit transaction
9. Return 200 OK with the deleted todo object including deletedAt timestamp

Error handling:
- 401 Unauthorized: No valid authentication token provided
- 404 Not Found: Todo does not exist or belongs to another user
- 409 Conflict: Todo is already deleted (in trash)
- 422 Unprocessable Entity: Invalid todoId format

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the todo to delete
parameters.name: todoId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of deleted todos (trash) belonging to the authenticated member.

This endpoint provides access to todos that have been soft-deleted by the user. Deleted todos are stored in a trash area where they remain visible to the owner but hidden from the normal todo list. Users can restore deleted todos from this location or permanently remove them.

The response includes only essential fields for trash display: the todo identifier, title, description, and the timestamp when the todo was deleted. Pagination is supported to efficiently handle large numbers of deleted todos.

Important: Users can only view their own deleted todos. The system enforces strict data isolation by filtering results to only include todos where user_id matches the authenticated member's ID.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query multi_user_todo_app_todos table filtered by deleted_at IS NOT NULL AND user_id = current_auth_user_id. Apply pagination with configurable page number and limit. Return only essential fields: id, title, description, and deletedAt timestamp. Sort by deleted_at descending (newest deletions first) by default. The authenticated member can only view their own deleted todos.

Pagination parameters:
- page: current page number (default 1, minimum 1)
- limit: items per page (default 10, maximum 100)

Security: Always filter by user_id to enforce data isolation. Never return todos belonging to other users.

Error handling: Return 404 if no deleted todos exist for the user. No query parameters for filtering by status or date range for trash - trash only contains deleted items.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of deleted todo summaries

operations.description:
Restore a deleted todo from trash back to the active todo list.

This operation reverses a soft delete by moving the specified todo from the trash collection back to the normal todo list. The todo's deletedAt timestamp is cleared, and it immediately becomes visible in the user's active todo list.

The restoring user must be the owner of the todo. The system validates that the todo exists in the trash (has a deletedAt timestamp) before performing the restoration. This prevents attempting to restore todos that have already been restored or permanently deleted.

When a todo is restored, all of its original data is preserved including:
- Title and description
- Start date and due date
- Completion status (isCompleted)
- Creation timestamp (createdAt)
- Complete edit history from previous states

The restored todo can then be edited, completed, deleted again, or have its edit history viewed just like any other active todo.

Related operations:
- GET /api/todos/trash - View all deleted todos before restoration
- GET /api/todos/{id} - View the restored todo in its active state
- DELETE /api/todos/{id} - Soft delete a todo to move it to trash
- DELETE /api/todos/{id} - Permanent deletion from trash (also deletes edit history)
operations.name: restore
operations.specification:
Implement todo restoration from trash by:

1. Extract todoId from path parameter
2. Verify user is authenticated (member actor)
3. Query multi_user_todo_app_todos for the todo with id = todoId
4. Validate todo exists and is owned by the authenticated user
5. Check todo is in trash (deletedAt is not null)
6. If todo not in trash or not owned by user, return 404 Not Found
7. Update the todo by setting deletedAt to null/undefined
8. Query the updated todo record to return full details
9. Return the restored todo with all fields

Error handling:
- 404 when todoId does not exist or does not belong to user
- 404 when todo is not in trash (already restored or permanently deleted)
- 401 when user is not authenticated

Database operations:
- Single UPDATE query on multi_user_todo_app_todos
- No new edit history entries created on restoration
- Edit history remains intact and accessible via GET /api/todos/{id}/history

responseBody.description: The fully restored todo with all fields intact

parameters.description: The ID of the todo to restore from trash
parameters.name: todoId

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete edit history for a specific todo.

This endpoint returns all edit history entries associated with the identified todo, sorted by edit timestamp in descending order (most recent changes first). Each history entry captures the state of fields before and after an edit, documenting what was changed during each modification.

The edit history provides an audit trail of all modifications made to the todo's title, description, start date, and due date fields. Users can view this history to track changes over time and understand how their todo has evolved.

Only the owner of the todo can access its edit history. This enforces data privacy and ensures users can only view changes to their own todos.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the multi_user_todo_app_todo_edit_histories table for all entries where todo_id matches the path parameter todoId.
Filter entries by ownership - only return history for todos owned by the authenticated member.
Join with multi_user_todo_app_todos to verify ownership via member_id relationship.
Order results by edited_at descending (most recent first).
Return paginated results with totalCount for cursor-based navigation.
Each response entry includes: id, editedAt timestamp, and old/new values for title, description, startDate, dueDate fields that were changed in that edit.
Handle UUID validation for todoId path parameter.
Return 404 if todo does not exist or user does not own the todo.
Return 401 if not authenticated.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of edit history entries for the todo

operations.description:
Permanently delete a todo from the trash, including all associated edit history entries.

This operation removes a todo from the system entirely when it exists in the trash (soft-deleted state). The todo will no longer be accessible through any API endpoint and cannot be recovered after this operation completes.

Before deleting the todo, the system verifies that the todo belongs to the authenticated user and is currently in the trash (has a deleted_at timestamp). The operation then deletes all edit history entries associated with the todo from the edit history table to ensure complete data removal.

Only the owner of the todo can perform this operation. Users cannot permanently delete todos that belong to other users or todos that have not been soft-deleted first (those must be moved to trash before permanent deletion).
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Verify authentication token is present in Authorization header.

Query multi_user_todo_app_todos table by id matching {todoId} parameter.

Validate that the todo exists and belongs to the authenticated user (member actor) by checking user_id foreign key.

Validate that the todo is in trash state by checking deleted_at column is not null.

Query multi_user_todo_app_todo_edit_histories table for all entries where todo_id matches the todo being deleted.

Execute database transaction:
  1. Delete all edit history entries for this todo (cascade delete not sufficient per business rules)
  2. Delete the todo record from multi_user_todo_app_todos

Commit transaction and return success response.

Rollback transaction if any error occurs during deletion.

Handle edge cases:
  - Todo not found: return 404 error
  - Todo not owned by authenticated user: return 403 error
  - Todo not in trash (deleted_at is null): return 400 error indicating todo must be soft-deleted first
