text: I'll now generate comprehensive E2E test suites for all the API endpoints we've defined. This will include test scenarios for authentication, user profiles, todo CRUD operations, trash functionality, filtering, sorting, and edit history.

instruction:
Authentication Tests:
- Test user signup with valid email, password, and display name
- Test user signup with invalid email format
- Test user signup with password less than 6 characters
- Test user signup with duplicate email
- Test user login with valid credentials
- Test user login with invalid credentials
- Test user login with non-existent email
- Test password change with valid current and new password
- Test password change with invalid current password
- Test account deletion (should delete user and all todos)

User Profile Tests:
- Test get current user profile
- Test update display name
- Test update display name with empty string
- Test that users cannot access other users' profiles

Todo Creation Tests:
- Test create todo with valid title
- Test create todo without description
- Test create todo with start and due dates
- Test create todo with empty description string
- Test create todo with invalid title (missing)

Todo List Tests:
- Test get todos list with default pagination
- Test get todos list with custom page and limit
- Test get todos list with completed filter
- Test get todos list with incomplete filter
- Test get todos list with all filter
- Test get todos list sorted by creation date (desc)
- Test get todos list sorted by creation date (asc)
- Test get todos list sorted by start date (ascending with nulls last)
- Test get todos list sorted by due date (descending with nulls last)
- Test that user cannot see other user's todos

Todo CRUD Tests:
- Test get single todo by ID
- Test get non-existent todo (should return 404)
- Test update todo title
- Test update todo description
- Test update todo dates
- Test update todo with all fields
- Test that updating creates edit history entry
- Test that user cannot update other user's todo

Todo Completion Tests:
- Test mark todo as complete
- Test mark complete todo as incomplete
- Test toggle completion status

Todo Deletion & Trash Tests:
- Test soft delete todo (should not appear in normal list)
- Test soft delete todo (should appear in trash list)
- Test restore todo from trash
- Test restore todo (should appear in normal list)
- Test permanent delete todo from trash
- Test permanent delete todo (should also delete edit history)
- Test restore non-existent todo (should return 404)

Edit History Tests:
- Test get edit history for todo
- Test that history is sorted by most recent first
- Test that history shows all field changes
- Test that permanent delete removes history entries

Privacy & Security Tests:
- Test that all authenticated endpoints require valid JWT token
- Test that unauthenticated requests return 401
- Test that users can only access their own resources
- Test that soft-deleted todos don't appear in normal todo list
- Test that permanently deleted todos can't be restored

Edge Case Tests:
- Test pagination edge cases (page 0, negative limit)
- Test sorting with todos that have no dates
- Test filtering when no todos match criteria
- Test update todo with partial fields

scenario.draft: Test successful guest registration with valid credentials. The test sends a POST request to /multiUserTodoApp/auth/guest/join with a valid email address (e.g., test@example.com), password with at least 6 characters (e.g., password123), display_name (e.g., Test User), href (e.g., http://localhost:3000/signup), and referrer (e.g., http://localhost:3000/). The system validates the email format against standard email validation patterns, checks email uniqueness against the multi_user_todo_app_guests table, hashes the password using bcrypt, creates a new guest record with the provided data, and generates a JWT session by creating a record in the multi_user_todo_app_guest_sessions table. The response includes the guest ID and authorization token containing access_token, refresh_token, and expired_at timestamp. The test validates that the account was created successfully, the password was properly hashed in the database, the JWT token was issued with proper expiration times, and the token structure matches the IAuthorizationToken schema with all required fields (access, refresh, expired_at, refreshable_until).

dependencies.purpose:
Essential authentication prerequisite:
This join operation (post /multiUserTodoApp/auth/guest/join) must be executed before any operations requiring 'guest' actor authorization.
It establishes the necessary user account and authentication context for the 'guest' actor, enabling subsequent API calls that depend on this specific authorization level.
Without this join operation, the main scenario endpoint and its dependencies will fail due to insufficient authentication credentials.

scenario.draft: Test guest registration with minimal valid data to verify the registration workflow handles required fields correctly. The test sends a POST request with a valid email, password meeting the minimum length requirement, a simple display_name, href, and referrer. This scenario verifies that the system successfully creates a guest account when all required fields (email, password, href, referrer) are provided with valid values. The test validates that the response contains a properly formatted guest ID, the authorization token structure is correct with all four required fields (access, refresh, expired_at, refreshable_until), and the newly created guest can immediately use the authentication token for subsequent API calls without requiring a separate login step.

scenario.draft: This scenario tests the successful guest session token refresh workflow. First, a guest account is created via registration to establish a valid session with access_token and refresh_token. The test then sends a refresh request with the valid refresh_token from the registration response. The system should validate the refresh token against the guest_sessions table, confirm it is not expired and is associated with an active guest account. Upon validation, the system creates a new session record with fresh access_token and refresh_token values, invalidates the old refresh token to prevent replay attacks, and returns the new authentication credentials. The test validates that the response contains a valid guest_id, new access token, new refresh token, and correct expiration timestamps. The old refresh token is verified to be unusable for subsequent refresh attempts.

scenario.draft: This scenario tests the refresh endpoint when provided with an expired refresh token. A guest account is created first to obtain an initial session with access_token and refresh_token. The test then simulates an expired refresh token by either using a token that has passed its refreshable_until timestamp or manually modifying the session record's expiration. The refresh request is sent with the expired token. The system should reject the request because the token is no longer valid for refresh. The test validates that the endpoint returns an appropriate error response indicating the token has expired or is invalid, and no new session is created.

First, register a new member account using /multiUserTodoApp/auth/member/join with a valid email address, password (6+ characters), and display name. Then authenticate using the same credentials via /multiUserTodoApp/auth/member/login. First, register a new member account using /multiUserTodoApp/auth/member/join with a valid email, password, and display name. Then attempt to login using /multiUserTodoApp/auth/member/login with the same email but a different (incorrect) password. Verify the system returns a 401 Unauthorized response. Confirm the error message is generic and does not reveal whether the email exists or password is wrong (security best practice). Ensure no new session tokens are created and the member remains unauthenticated. Verify that subsequent authenticated API calls fail with 401 Unauthorized.

scenario.draft: Test login failure when attempting to authenticate with a non-existent email address. First, create a valid user account via POST /multiUserTodoApp/auth/member/join with a real email address (e.g., existing_user@example.com) - this establishes a known registered user in the system. Then, attempt to login via POST /multiUserTodoApp/auth/member/login using a DIFFERENT email address that has never been registered (e.g., fake_user@example.com). Provide any password value (it will be ignored since the email doesn't exist). Verify the system returns a 401 Unauthorized response. Confirm the error message is generic and indistinguishable from the invalid password case (does not reveal whether email exists). This prevents email enumeration attacks. Ensure no session tokens are generated and no database sessions are created for this non-existent account. This validates that the system does not leak information about account existence through different error messages or response times.

text: I'll now implement the actual business logic for all the API endpoints. This will include service providers for authentication, user profiles, todo CRUD operations, trash management, and edit history tracking.

instruction:
Implement all API endpoint service logic:

Authentication Services:
- authService.signup(): Create new user account with email, password, and display name. Hash password, create user and profile in same transaction. Return JWT token.
- authService.login(): Validate email and password, return JWT token.
- authService.changePassword(): Verify current password, update to new password.
- authService.deleteAccount(): Delete user profile and all their todos (including trash), return success.

Profile Services:
- profileService.getProfile(): Get current user's profile.
- profileService.updateProfile(): Update user's display name.

Todo Services:
- todoService.createTodo(): Create new todo with title, description, dates. Set isCompleted=false.
- todoService.getTodos(): List todos with pagination, filtering by status, and sorting. Handle null date sorting.
- todoService.getTodo(): Get single todo by ID (ensure it belongs to user).
- todoService.updateTodo(): Update todo fields, create edit history entry.
- todoService.toggleComplete(): Toggle completion status.
- todoService.softDeleteTodo(): Set deleted_at timestamp.
- todoService.restoreTodo(): Clear deleted_at timestamp.
- todoService.permanentDeleteTodo(): Delete todo and all its history entries.

Trash Services:
- trashService.getTrash(): List deleted todos with pagination.

Edit History Services:
- historyService.getHistory(): Get todo's edit history sorted by edited_at desc.
- historyService.createEntry(): Create history entry when todo is edited.

Business Logic Rules:
- All authenticated endpoints must verify JWT token and extract user_id
- Users can only access their own todos (filter by user_id)
- Soft delete: deleted_at is null for active, non-null for trash
- Hard delete: removes todo and all history entries
- Edit history must capture old and new values for each field changed
- Sorting with null dates: nulls appear last
- Password hashing before storing
- Transaction for signup (user + profile) and account deletion
- JWT token generation for auth responses

Validation Rules:
- Email format validation
- Password minimum 6 characters
- Title required and cannot be empty
- Pagination: page >= 1, limit >= 1, limit <= 100
- Sorting fields: createdAt, startDate, dueDate
- Sort orders: asc, desc
- Status filter: all, completed, incomplete

TypeScript compilation error found in src/MyGlobal.ts: Cannot find module './MyConfiguration' or its corresponding type declarations. This is a dependency import error that prevents the entire authorization system from compiling. The MyGlobal.ts file is trying to import configuration data that doesn't exist in the project yet.

Component Breakdown:
- MyGlobal.ts: Missing MyConfiguration import
- memberAuthorize.ts: Depends on MyGlobal and jwtAuthorize
- MemberAuth.ts: Depends on memberAuthorize
- MemberPayload.ts: Standalone type definition
authorizations.solution_guidance:
1. Create src/MyConfiguration.ts file with proper exports for database connection and JWT configuration
2. Ensure jwtAuthorize.ts exists in src/providers/authorize/ with proper JWT token verification logic
3. Ensure MemberPayload.ts exists with proper UUID format tags
4. All three components (memberAuthorize, MemberAuth, MemberPayload) will be generated with correct import paths
5. The MyGlobal.ts file needs to import from the newly created MyConfiguration.ts
